sessions.title: Revision River Ferry Ending Route
sessions.sessionFit: Adult-led 25-minute after-school story club session for an older writing table after snack or homework time.
sessions.directorSetup: Print one session page per writer, set pencils at each seat, place three draft-route cards in the center, and leave a quiet finish basket on the side table.
sessions.kidDirection: Choose one rough ending, ferry it past two helpful details, and write a clearer final line for an invented scene.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Ask which early detail should return at the end and what the reader should understand at the final dock.

pageSections.heading: Starting Dock
lines: The early detail waiting on the dock is ____________________.
The scene changes when ____________________.
The rough ending I want to improve is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Ferry Revision
lines: One word I can remove for clarity is ____________________.
One detail I can carry forward is ____________________.
The ending becomes easier to follow because ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Final Dock
lines: My revised ending begins with ____________________.
The detail that echoes the start is ____________________.
The final dock leaves readers thinking about ____________________.

sessions.clubShareLine: Share the echoed detail you used, or point to it on the page: ____________________.
sessions.wrapUpLine: The ending choice I improved today was ____________________.
sessions.quietOptionLine: Work silently by writing only the revised final sentence here: ____________________.
sessions.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one ending revision detail for this club story: ____________________.

sessions.title: Clue Label Tower Focus Label
sessions.sessionFit: Adult-led 30-minute after-school story club session for older writers building one concise exhibit paragraph.
sessions.directorSetup: Print the pages, set out pencils, place three harmless object cards on each table, and mark a display corner for finished paper labels.
sessions.kidDirection: Invent a tower exhibit, choose the clue that matters most, and write a label that guides readers in a clear order.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Ask which clue belongs first, which detail can wait, and how the label can stay short but useful.

pageSections.heading: Tower Exhibit
lines: The object on the tower shelf is ____________________.
The clue beside it shows ____________________.
A detail that can wait for another label is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Label Order
lines: Readers should notice first that ____________________.
The middle sentence should explain ____________________.
The final sentence should point toward ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Curator Finish
lines: The clearest label word I used is ____________________.
One word I can replace for focus is ____________________.
My finished tower label says ____________________.

sessions.clubShareLine: Share one clue word that helped your label stay focused: ____________________.
sessions.wrapUpLine: The detail I chose to leave out was ____________________.
sessions.quietOptionLine: Skip sharing and copy your final label neatly here: ____________________.
sessions.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one focused detail selection detail for this club story: ____________________.

sessions.title: Compass Craft Academy Paragraph Route
sessions.sessionFit: Adult-led 25-minute after-school story club session for planning a beginning, turn, and finish before drafting.
sessions.directorSetup: Print one page per writer, draw three route dots on a board or chart paper, and set route-word cards near the table edge.
sessions.kidDirection: Map a paragraph route for a made-up compass craft, then write the sentence that moves readers through the turn.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Ask which sentence acts like the compass needle and keeps the paragraph pointed forward.

pageSections.heading: Route Dots
lines: The paragraph starts beside ____________________.
The route turns when ____________________.
The finish should show readers ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Compass Sentence
lines: A word that moves the route forward is ____________________.
A phrase that explains the turn is ____________________.
The sentence that guides readers best is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Academy Finish
lines: The route detail I can make clearer is ____________________.
The final sentence should connect back to ____________________.
My compass craft paragraph line is ____________________.

sessions.clubShareLine: Share the route word that helped your paragraph turn: ____________________.
sessions.wrapUpLine: The sentence that shaped my paragraph was ____________________.
sessions.quietOptionLine: Work quietly by tracing three route dots and writing the turn here: ____________________.
sessions.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one paragraph structure detail for this club story: ____________________.

sessions.title: Almost Invention Workshop Test Note
sessions.sessionFit: Adult-led 30-minute after-school story club session for older writers who need a structured explain-and-revise task.
sessions.directorSetup: Print the workshop pages, set pencils and three step cards at each table, and keep all invention ideas on paper with no real building required.
sessions.kidDirection: Describe an almost-invention, put its steps in a sensible order, and write a test note that explains what to adjust next.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Ask where a reader might get confused and which step should be moved, shortened, or clarified.

pageSections.heading: Workshop Plan
lines: The almost-invention is supposed to help with ____________________.
The first harmless part on the bench is ____________________.
The part that needs a clearer job is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Step Order
lines: The first instruction should tell readers to ____________________.
The step that belongs next is ____________________.
The step that needs clearer wording is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Test Note
lines: The invention almost works when ____________________.
The adjustment I would try next is ____________________.
My workshop test note says ____________________.

sessions.clubShareLine: Share one step you moved or clarified for readers: ____________________.
sessions.wrapUpLine: The instruction I made clearest today was ____________________.
sessions.quietOptionLine: Work silently by revising one step and writing it here: ____________________.
sessions.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one instruction order detail for this club story: ____________________.

sessions.title: Margin Note Market Kind Feedback
sessions.sessionFit: Adult-led 25-minute after-school story club session for practicing useful revision comments on invented sample lines.
sessions.directorSetup: Print the pages, place pencils and sample note strips on each table, and use only invented writing snippets for the feedback practice.
sessions.kidDirection: Trade a fuzzy market note for a kind, specific revision task, then write a new line that follows the note.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Ask which exact word, detail, or order change would make the note useful without making it personal.

pageSections.heading: Market Note
lines: The fuzzy note on the stand says ____________________.
The note feels too broad because ____________________.
A kinder version of the note could start with ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Revision Trade
lines: The detail I want the writer to add is ____________________.
The plain word I would trade out is ____________________.
The sentence would be easier to follow if ____________________.

pageSections.heading: New Story Line
lines: My revised story line begins with ____________________.
The clearer detail readers can notice is ____________________.
The next useful note could be about ____________________.

sessions.clubShareLine: Share one feedback phrase that stayed kind and specific: ____________________.
sessions.wrapUpLine: The revision move I can explain clearly is ____________________.
sessions.quietOptionLine: Work quietly by choosing one note and writing only the revised line: ____________________.
sessions.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one specific feedback detail for this club story: ____________________.

sessions.title: Index Card Theater Scene Turn
sessions.sessionFit: Adult-led 30-minute after-school story club session for shaping a small scene with a clear shift.
sessions.directorSetup: Print the pages, set pencils at each seat, place three scene cards face up, and keep the share time optional for quieter writers.
sessions.kidDirection: Arrange three theater cards, write a two-line exchange, and make the second line change the direction of the scene.
sessions.facilitatorPrompt: Ask what the first speaker expects, what the reply changes, and which stage action makes the turn clear.

pageSections.heading: Scene Cards
lines: The first scene card shows ____________________.
The middle card changes the plan because ____________________.
The final card should reveal ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Dialogue Turn
lines: The first line of dialogue is ____________________.
The reply changes the scene when ____________________.
A small stage action between the lines is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Theater Finish
lines: The turning point becomes clear because ____________________.
One cue word I can revise is ____________________.
My final theater scene line is ____________________.

sessions.clubShareLine: Share the line or action that turned your scene: ____________________.
sessions.wrapUpLine: The moment that changed my scene most was ____________________.
sessions.quietOptionLine: Skip read-aloud time and write your strongest scene line here: ____________________.
sessions.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Add one scene turning point detail for this club story: ____________________.
